cards.en:
Encryption is a process of transforming data into an unreadable form with a key. Its main purpose is to ensure data privacy in case the data is hacked or accessed illegally. Decryption is the reverse process of encryption: the encrypted data is converted back to its original form using the corresponding key.

Key point for exams: encryption does not prevent interception. A hacker can still capture, copy or even delete the packets. What encryption prevents is the readable content from being interpreted by anyone without the correct key.

Encryption is used whenever confidential data travels over an untrusted network: online banking, HTTPS web pages, VPN tunnels, Wi-Fi (WPA2), instant messaging (end-to-end encryption) and stored backups.
cards.zh:
Encryption（加密）：用 key 把数据变成不可读的形式，目的是 ensure data privacy，即使数据被入侵或非法存取也读不懂。Decryption（解密）是相反过程，用对应的 key 把数据还原。

考试重点：encryption does not prevent interception——黑客仍可截取、复制甚至删除数据，只是读不懂内容。所以选择题问“加密的作用”，正确答案是 “hackers cannot read the messages easily”，不是 “cannot collect / edit / delete”。

应用：网上银行、HTTPS、VPN、Wi-Fi WPA2、即时通讯 end-to-end encryption、加密备份。

ex.q: A student says: 'After I encrypt my email, hackers can no longer intercept it.' Is this correct?
ex.a: No. Encryption does not stop interception; packets can still be captured. It only makes the captured ciphertext unreadable without the decryption key, so the content stays private.
ex.az: 不正确。加密不能阻止截取，只令截到的密文读不懂。

cards.en:
Plaintext is the original readable message. Ciphertext is the unreadable result after encryption. The sender uses an encryption key to convert plaintext into ciphertext; the recipient uses a decryption key to convert ciphertext back into plaintext. A key is actually a string of numbers and characters used by the encryption algorithm.

A simple classroom example is a substitution table: each plaintext character is replaced by the character in the same column of a ciphertext row. The table (or the shift amount in a Caesar cipher) acts as the key. As long as the method/key is unknown to others, a third party cannot interpret the message, e.g. 'I love ICT' → 'L$oryh$LFW' (shift by 3).
cards.zh:
Plaintext（明文）= 原本可读的讯息；Ciphertext（密文）= 加密后不可读的结果。发送者用 encryption key 把明文变密文，接收者用 decryption key 还原。Key 其实是 a string of numbers and characters。

课本活动用 substitution table（替换表）：每个字母换成同一栏的密文字元；Caesar cipher 则把每个字母移位固定数目，移位数就是 key。只要别人不知道方法/key，就读不懂。例：'I love ICT' 每字母后移 3 → 'L oryh LFW'。

ex.q: Encrypt 'ICT' with a Caesar cipher of shift 3, then decrypt 'KHOOR'.
ex.a:
Shift each letter forward 3: I→L, C→F, T→W, so ciphertext = LFW.
Decrypt by shifting back 3: K→H, H→E, O→L, O→L, R→O → HELLO.
ex.az: 加密每字母后移 3 得 LFW；解密每字母前移 3 得 HELLO。

cards.en:
The size (number of bits) of the key is related to the degree of security. An n-bit key has 2n possible key combinations. A hacker without the key must try every combination (brute-force attack), which takes a great deal of time.

Maximum time to crack = 2n ÷ (keys tried per second).

Therefore a longer key is more secure because there are more combinations, so hackers need more time to crack the message. Trade-off: a longer key needs more computation time to encrypt and decrypt. Note that encrypted data does not simply become 'longer' or 'more packets'; the security comes from the number of possible keys.
cards.zh:
Key 的位元数决定安全程度：n-bit key 有 2n 个可能组合。没有 key 的黑客只能逐个尝试（brute force）。
最长破解时间 = 2n ÷ 每秒尝试次数。

所以 128-bit 比 64-bit 安全：组合多 264 倍，黑客需要更长时间。代价是加解密运算时间较长。注意答案要写 “hackers need more time to crack”，不是“数据变长/packet 变多”。

ex.q: A program tries 2000 keys per second. Find the maximum time to crack (a) a 16-bit key, (b) a 32-bit key.
Why is a 128-bit key more secure than a 64-bit key?
ex.a: It has 2<sup>128</sup> instead of 2<sup>64</sup> combinations (2<sup>64</sup> times more), so a brute-force attack needs far more time.
ex.az: 组合数多 2^64 倍，暴力破解需要的时间大大增加。

cards.en:
Private key encryption, also known as symmetric key encryption, uses the same key for both encryption and decryption. The key must be exchanged beforehand and kept private. The sender encrypts with the key and the recipient decrypts with the same key.

Advantages: simple and fast, suitable for large amounts of data.
Problems: (1) how to transfer the key securely to the recipient — if it is intercepted, all messages can be read; (2) key management becomes difficult when there are many users, since every pair of users needs its own secret key: n users need n(n−1)/2 keys.
cards.zh:
Private key encryption = symmetric key encryption：加密和解密用同一把 key。Key 要预先交换并保密。

优点：简单、快，适合大量数据。
问题：(1) 如何安全地把 key 交给对方——key 被截取就全部泄密；(2) 用户多时 key management 困难：每两人需一把 key，n 人需 n(n−1)/2 把。这正是 public key encryption 要解决的问题。

ex.q: A class of 10 students each want a separate secret symmetric key with every other student. How many keys are needed?
ex.a: Each pair needs one key: n(n−1)/2 = 10×9/2 = 45 keys. This shows why key management is difficult with symmetric encryption.
ex.az: 10×9÷2 = 45 把，说明对称加密的 key 管理困难。

cards.tz: 公开密码匙（不对称）加密
cards.en:
Public key encryption, also known as asymmetric key encryption, uses a pair of keys: a public key available to everyone and a private key that is confidential and kept by the owner only. They work in pairs and are unique for each user. A message encrypted with either key must be decrypted by the other key of the pair.

It solves the key-distribution problem: the public key can be published freely, and no secret key needs to be sent. It is used in two modes: encryption mode (privacy) and authentication mode (digital signature). It is slower than symmetric encryption, so in practice (e.g. SSL) it is often used to exchange a symmetric session key.
cards.zh:
Public key encryption = asymmetric key encryption：每个用户有一对 key——public key（公开给所有人）与 private key（只有自己持有、保密）。用其中一把加密，就必须用同一对的另一把解密。

好处：公钥可公开，毋须安全传送秘密 key，解决对称加密的派发问题。两种模式：encryption mode（保密）与 authentication mode（数码签署）。缺点是运算较慢。

ex.q: Mary encrypted a file with her own public key. Who can decrypt it?
ex.a: Only the matching key of the pair can decrypt: Mary's private key, so only Mary can read it.
ex.az: 只有同一对的 Mary 私钥能解密，即只有 Mary 本人。

cards.en:
Encryption mode: the sender encrypts with the recipient's public key; only the designated recipient can decrypt with their own private key. Anyone can send, only one can read → privacy/confidentiality. Suitable for online banking and any secured data transmission.

Authentication mode: the sender encrypts (signs) with their own private key; any recipient can decrypt with the sender's public key. Since only the sender holds the private key, successful decryption verifies the identity of the sender. This is the basis for digital signatures.

Memory rule: keep it secret → recipient's public key; prove who sent it → sender's private key.
cards.zh:
Encryption mode：用收件人的 public key 加密，只有收件人用自己的 private key 能解密 → 保密（网银、成绩单）。
Authentication mode：用寄件人自己的 private key 加密（签署），任何人用寄件人的 public key 解密 → 证明寄件人身份，是 digital signature 的基础（学校通告）。

口诀：要保密 → 收件人公钥；要证明是谁发 → 寄件人私钥。

ex.q: For each case choose the key the sender uses: (a) secondary school sends a verified ECA record to a university; (b) helpers send drug-use questionnaires to an organisation; (c) student sends credit card number to a merchant; (d) parent digitally signs a reply slip to the school.
ex.a:
(a) Purpose is proving the source → secondary school's private key.
(b) Confidential → organisation's public key.
(c) Confidential → merchant's public key.
(d) Signature → parent's private key.
ex.az: (a) 学校私钥（证明来源）；(b) 机构公钥（保密）；(c) 商户公钥；(d) 家长私钥（签署）。

cards.t: Public Key Infrastructure and Certification Authority
cards.tz: 公开密码匙基础建设与核证机关
cards.en:
How can we be sure a public key really belongs to the claimed person and is not forged? Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) is a network security architecture based on public key encryption, relying on publicly recognised Certification Authorities (CA).

The main role of a CA is to act as a publicly trusted third party to issue and manage digital certificates. A digital certificate is a digital document linked to a public key which verifies whether an individual or organisation owns that public key. Applicants must provide documentary proof of identity; the CA then signs the certificate.

In Hong Kong, Hongkong Post is the first recognised CA under the Electronic Transactions Ordinance (ETO, Cap. 553), issuing e-Cert, Bank-Cert and iAM Smart-Cert; Digi-Sign is the other recognised CA. Under the ETO, a digital signature supported by a recognised certificate has the same legal status as a handwritten signature.
cards.zh:
如何确定公钥真的属于对方、不是伪造？PKI 是建基于 public key encryption 的保安架构，依靠公认的 Certification Authority (CA)。
CA 是公众信任的第三方，负责签发及管理 digital certificates。Digital certificate 是连结 public key 的数码文件，证明该公钥属于某人/机构；申请时需提交身份证明。

香港：Hongkong Post 是 Electronic Transactions Ordinance（ETO, Cap. 553）下首个认可 CA，发出 e-Cert、Bank-Cert、iAM Smart-Cert；另一个是 Digi-Sign。用认可证书的 digital signature 与手写签名有同等法律效力。

ex.q: Mary and Bob both hold digital certificates in the HK PKI. What can Bob retrieve from the PKI system to send Mary a confidential message?
ex.a: Bob retrieves Mary's digital certificate / public key (never her private key). He encrypts with Mary's public key so only Mary's private key can decrypt.
ex.az: Bob 只能取得 Mary 的证书及公钥（私钥永不公开），用它加密。

cards.en:
Using both key pairs together, the sender encrypts the message using the recipient's public key and signs it using their own private key; the recipient verifies using the sender's public key and decrypts using their own private key. This achieves:
  1. Privacy – only the designated recipient can decrypt.
  2. Authentication – if the message can be verified with the sender's public key, it was signed by the owner of the private key.
  3. Integrity – if the message is modified after signing, it can no longer be verified by the sender's public key, so successful verification means it was not changed.
  4. Non-repudiation – the result of authentication + integrity: the sender cannot deny having sent the message.
cards.zh:
同时使用两对 key：寄件人用收件人公钥加密，再用自己私钥签署；收件人用寄件人公钥验证，再用自己私钥解密。达成 PAIN：
1. Privacy：只有收件人可解密。
2. Authentication：能用寄件人公钥验证 → 确认是他签署。
3. Integrity：签署后被改动就验证失败 → 成功即未被修改。
4. Non-repudiation：由 authentication + integrity 得出，寄件人不能否认曾发送。

ex.q: How can PKI prevent eavesdropping and also stop a sender later denying an order?
ex.a:
Eavesdropping: encrypt with the recipient's public key, so intercepted ciphertext can only be decrypted by the recipient's private key (privacy).
Denial: the sender signs with his private key; verification with his public key proves he sent it and that it was not altered, so he cannot deny it (non-repudiation).
ex.az: 用收件人公钥加密防窃听；寄件人用私钥签署，验证成功证明身份及未被修改，不能抵赖。

cards.en:
Authentication in access control is a network security and privacy measure used to verify the user's identity. Only authorised users have the credentials to log in. Common methods: username and password, token, smart card, biometrics, digital certificate and two-factor authentication.

Username and password is the most common practice. It is convenient and cheap to implement, but the strength of the password affects the degree of network security: weak passwords can be guessed or cracked, and passwords can be stolen by phishing, keyloggers or shoulder-surfing. Some systems use security questions instead of (or in addition to) passwords, but these are still 'something you know'.
cards.zh:
Authentication（认证）：用来核实用户身份的保安措施，只有获授权者有登入凭证。方法：username & password、token、smart card、biometrics、digital certificate、2FA。

Username and password 最常用，方便、成本低，但安全程度取决于密码强度；密码可被猜中、破解、phishing、keylogger 或偷看。有些系统用 security questions，但仍属 “something you know”。

ex.q: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of using only username and password for a school portal.
ex.a:
Advantage: convenient, no extra device or cost.
Disadvantage: if the password is weak or stolen (e.g. by phishing), anyone can log in as the student.
ex.az: 优点：方便、无额外成本；缺点：密码弱或被盗就可冒认登入。

cards.en:
A token is a security device used to authenticate a user, like an electronic key.
• Hard token: a small electronic authentication hardware device (e.g. a bank security device).
• Soft token: software with a private key installed in a computer or smartphone; the key is encrypted and stored in a keystore.

Since a token can easily be lost, users often enter a password to activate it. The token then generates a one-time password (OTP). Each OTP can only be used once and becomes invalid after a short time, which protects users from password guessing attacks and replay of stolen passwords. Misconception: the OTP is generated by the token locally, not sent into the token by the server.

A connected token must be physically connected (USB, NFC, Bluetooth) and transmits the authentication data automatically.
cards.zh:
Token（权标）：认证用的保安装置，像电子锁匙。
• Hard token：小型硬件（银行保安编码器）。
• Soft token：装在电脑/手机的软件，内含加密储存于 keystore 的 private key。

Token 易遗失，常要先输入密码启动，再产生 OTP。每个 OTP 只能用一次，短时间后失效 → 防 password guessing 及被偷后重用。误解：OTP 是 token 本身产生，不是由 server 传入。
Connected token 需实体连接（USB、NFC、Bluetooth），自动传送认证资料。

ex.q: Joe's bank asks for a 6-digit OTP from his security token after the password. Why?
ex.a: It adds a second factor (something he holds). A stolen password alone is useless, and each OTP is valid only once for a short time, so an intercepted OTP cannot be reused.
ex.az: 加入第二个因素；单靠被盗密码无法登入，且 OTP 一次性、短时间失效，截取了也不能重用。

cards.en:
A smart card is one of the hard tokens. The chip of a smart card stores encrypted information or the private key of the card holder. The user inserts or taps the card on a reader to authenticate.

Examples: the new smart Hong Kong Identity Card (e-Channel immigration), the Octopus card used for electronic payment and for access control in schools and buildings, and bank smart cards that combine a bank card with a security token. Smart cards are convenient, but if lost and not protected by a PIN, someone else may use them, so they are often combined with a PIN.
cards.zh:
Smart card 是一种 hard token，芯片储存加密资料或持卡人的 private key。插入或拍卡于读卡器认证。
例子：新智能身份证（e-道）、八达通（电子支付及学校门禁）、结合银行卡与 security token 的银行智能卡。方便，但遗失后若无 PIN 保护可被他人使用，所以常配合 PIN。

ex.q: A school uses Octopus cards for gate access. State one weakness and an improvement.
ex.a:
Weakness: a lost/borrowed card lets another person enter (it only proves 'something you hold').
Improvement: add a second factor such as face recognition or a PIN.
ex.az: 弱点：卡被借/遗失可冒用；改善：加上人脸识别或 PIN 成为 2FA。

cards.en:
Biometrics identifies a person relying on the unique physical attributes of human beings. Common types:
• Fingerprint – unique patterns of the derma on a finger.
• Retina scan – patterns of blood vessels on the retina.
• Iris scan – patterns of the iris.
• Facial recognition – features such as eye width and nose.
• Voice recognition – characteristics of the vocal tract shape.
• Signature recognition (behavioural) – tilt of pen, pressure and time used.

Advantages: nothing to remember or carry, hard to forge or share. Risks: biometric data is extremely sensitive — once leaked it cannot be 'reset' like a password. Data users should collect the minimum data for one single purpose (e.g. identity authentication only).
Misconception: voice recognition (who is speaking, for authentication) is not the same as speech recognition (what is said).
cards.zh:
Biometrics：依靠人类独特的身体特征识别身份。指纹（真皮纹路）、视网膜（血管）、虹膜、人脸（眼距、鼻）、声纹（vocal tract shape）、签名（笔的倾斜、压力、时间，属行为特征）。

优点：不用记、不用带、难伪造。风险：生物特征资料极敏感，外泄后不能像密码一样重设；收集者应只收集最少资料、只用于单一目的。
误解：voice recognition（认出是谁）≠ speech recognition（认出说什么）。

ex.q: Why should a gym think carefully before collecting members' fingerprints for entry?
ex.a: Fingerprints are highly sensitive personal data; if leaked they cannot be changed like a password. The gym should consider whether it is necessary, collect only the minimum, use it only for entry, and secure it.
ex.az: 指纹外泄不能重设；应考虑是否必要、最少收集、只作入场用途并妥善保护。

cards.t: Digital certificates for authentication and iAM Smart
cards.tz: 数码证书认证与智方便
cards.en:
A recognised digital certificate is issued by a recognised CA to confirm the identity of the parties in an electronic transaction. In Hong Kong the two recognised CAs are Hongkong Post Certification Authority and Digi-Sign Certification Services.

The iAM Smart (智方便) platform, launched in 2020, gives citizens a digital identity: one-stop login to government and commercial online services, form auto-filling and digital signing with a legally recognised signature. Because the certificate is bound to the person's identity, websites can trust that the user is genuine.
cards.zh:
认可 CA 签发的 digital certificate 用来确认交易双方身份。香港两个认可 CA：香港邮政核证机关及 Digi-Sign。
iAM Smart（智方便）2020 年推出：一站式登入政府及商业网上服务、自动填表、数码签署（具法律效力）。证书与本人身份绑定，所以网站可信任用户身份。

ex.q: Which authentication method lets a citizen sign a government form online with legal effect?
ex.a: Using a recognised digital certificate, e.g. iAM Smart / e-Cert, to create a digital signature recognised under the ETO.
ex.az: 用认可数码证书（智方便、e-Cert）作数码签署。

cards.en:
Two-factor authentication (2FA) refers to the combined use of two different authentication factors to verify user identity, e.g. something you know (username and password) plus something you hold (mobile phone, token) or something you are (fingerprint).

Why safer: although hackers may steal a user's password via the Internet, it is very difficult for them to steal 'something you hold' via the Internet. Common forms: approve the login on a phone notification, enter a code from SMS or an authenticator app, or use biometrics.

Misconception: dual password authentication is NOT 2FA, because both passwords are the same factor (something you know).
cards.zh:
2FA：结合两种不同的认证因素，例如 know（密码）+ hold（手机、token）或 are（指纹）。
较安全的原因：黑客可经 Internet 偷密码，但很难经 Internet 偷走你手上的东西。形式：手机通知确认、SMS/authenticator 验证码、生物识别。
误解：两个密码不是 2FA，因为同属 something you know。

ex.q: Classify: (a) password + PIN; (b) password + fingerprint; (c) smart card + PIN.
ex.a: (a) Not 2FA – both 'know'. (b) 2FA – know + are. (c) 2FA – hold + know.
ex.az: (a) 不是；(b) 是（know+are）；(c) 是（hold+know）。

cards.t: SSL / TLS encryption in online transactions
cards.tz: 网上交易的 SSL/TLS 加密
cards.en:
Using HTTP to transmit confidential information in plain text is not safe. Secure Sockets Layer (SSL), known as Transport Layer Security (TLS), establishes an authenticated and encrypted communication link between clients and servers using public key encryption. If the page is encrypted by SSL and transferred using HTTPS, users can safely transmit credit card numbers and login credentials. The browser shows https:// and a lock icon.

Before logging in to online banking, click the lock icon to check the digital (SSL) certificate to confirm the website's identity (issued by a CA to the real bank, not expired) — this helps detect phishing sites. An SSL certificate enables an encrypted connection; it does not prevent computer viruses.
Misconception: HTTPS does not secure data stored in the database — SSL only applies during the data transmission process.
cards.zh:
用 HTTP 以明文传送机密资料不安全。SSL（即 TLS）用 public key encryption 在 client 与 server 之间建立已认证且加密的通讯连线。网页用 SSL 加密并经 HTTPS 传送，便可安全传送信用卡号码和登入资料；浏览器显示 https:// 和锁头。
登入网银前按锁头检查 SSL 证书，确认网站身份，防 phishing。SSL 证书不能防病毒。
误解：HTTPS 不保护数据库内的数据，SSL 只在传输过程中有效。

ex.q: Why do we need SSL when using online banking, and what does it NOT protect?
ex.a: SSL encrypts data during transmission so intercepted login details/transactions cannot be read, and the certificate authenticates the bank's website. It does not protect data already stored on the server or stop malware on the user's computer.
ex.az: SSL 加密传输中的数据并认证网站；不保护伺服器已储存的数据，也不防用户电脑中毒。

cards.t: Digital certificate and digital signature in transactions
cards.tz: 交易中的数码证书与数码签署
cards.en:
In online transactions, digital certificates let users verify the identity of websites (SSL certificate) and let banks/merchants verify customers (e.g. e-Cert). A digital signature is created by encrypting (signing) with the sender's private key backed by a digital certificate; it proves authenticity, integrity and non-repudiation.

Misconception: 'Digital signature is also called electronic signature' is wrong. An electronic signature is any signature in electronic form (a scanned handwritten signature, signing on a tablet, typing a name). A digital signature is a specific cryptographic technique using PKI.
cards.zh:
网上交易中，digital certificate 让用户核实网站身份（SSL 证书），亦让银行核实客户（e-Cert）。Digital signature 由寄件人用私钥签署并有证书支持，提供 authenticity、integrity、non-repudiation。
误解：digital signature 不等于 electronic signature。Electronic signature 泛指任何电子形式签名（扫描签名、平板手写）；digital signature 是运用 PKI 的加密技术。

ex.q: Is signing your name on a tablet at a bank counter a digital signature?
ex.a: No. It is an electronic signature (an image of a handwritten signature). A digital signature requires signing with a private key and a digital certificate.
ex.az: 不是，那是 electronic signature；digital signature 要用私钥及数码证书。

cards.t: 2FA in online transactions: token, SMS OTP, QR code
cards.en:
Most high-risk online transactions use 2FA:
• Security token: after logging in with username and password, the user enters the OTP generated by the token to gain full access. The token also offers transaction signing: the user keys in transaction data (e.g. the payee account number) to generate a matching security code. A smart card can combine a bank card with a security token.
• Mobile SMS OTP: the bank sends an OTP to the user's registered mobile phone; it can be used only once and expires shortly. The uniqueness of SIM cards lets the phone act as a security token, so no extra device is needed.
• QR code: the payment page shows a QR code that the user scans with the digital wallet app on their phone to confirm.

Good practices: prefer a wired network to public wireless, use strong passwords and change them regularly, scan only trusted QR codes (check for stickers placed over the real code).
cards.zh:
高风险网上交易多用 2FA：
• Security token：登入后输入 token 产生的 OTP；亦有 transaction signing（输入收款户口号码等产生对应编码）。Smart card 可结合银行卡及 token。
• SMS OTP：银行把 OTP 发到已登记手机，一次性、短时间失效；SIM 卡的唯一性令手机可当 token，不用另带装置。
• QR code：付款页显示 QR code，用手机电子钱包扫描确认。
良好习惯：用有线网络而非公共 Wi-Fi、强密码并定期更换、只扫可信 QR code（留意有否被贴上假贴纸）。

ex.q: State one advantage and one disadvantage of SMS OTP compared with a hard token.
ex.a:
Advantage: no extra device to carry; the phone (unique SIM) acts as the token.
Disadvantage: needs mobile signal; SMS may be intercepted or SIM swapped; a lost phone gives access to OTPs.
ex.az: 优点：毋须另带装置；缺点：需要讯号，SMS 可被截取或 SIM 被盗换，手机遗失有风险。

cards.en:
There are three basic authentication factors:
• Something you KNOW – password, PIN, security questions.
• Something you HOLD – token, smart card, mobile phone.
• Something you ARE – fingerprint, facial scan, voiceprint.

The greater the number of factors verified, the higher the degree of authentication. Two factors = 2FA; all three = three-factor authentication. Trade-off: more factors increase security but make logging in slower and require more equipment/cost, so systems choose the number of factors according to risk.
cards.zh:
三种基本认证因素：KNOW（密码、PIN、保安问题）、HOLD（token、smart card、手机）、ARE（指纹、人脸、声纹）。
验证的因素愈多，认证程度愈高。两个 = 2FA，三个 = three-factor。代价：较麻烦、需更多设备与成本，所以按风险决定用多少因素。

ex.q: A data centre door needs a staff card, a PIN and a fingerprint. How many factors? Name them.
ex.a: Three-factor authentication: card = something you hold, PIN = something you know, fingerprint = something you are.
ex.az: 三重：卡（hold）、PIN（know）、指纹（are）。

cards.en:
AI systems collect and analyse the user's login pattern — location/region, time of login, IP address, device. If irregularities are found, the system applies a stronger authentication mechanism than usual, protecting users without making daily logins troublesome (adaptive authentication):
• correct password, same region, regular time, known IP → login with no further step;
• correct password, different region of the country → two-factor authentication;
• correct password, different country, irregular time, never-seen IP → advanced multi-factor authentication.

AI can also use behavioural biometrics such as cursor movement and typing speed/patterns to recognise users automatically, reducing login complexity and the risk of compromised credentials.
cards.zh:
AI 收集并分析用户登入模式（地区、时间、IP、装置）。发现异常就要求比平常更强的认证：
• 同区、平常时间、熟悉 IP → 直接登入；
• 国内不同地区 → 2FA；
• 不同国家、异常时间、从未见过的 IP → 进阶 MFA。
亦可用 behavioural biometrics（滑鼠移动、打字速度与节奏）自动识别用户，减少登入麻烦并降低凭证被盗风险。

ex.q: Sam usually logs in from Hong Kong at 8 pm. Today the correct password is entered from overseas at 4 am from a new IP. What should an AI system do and why?
ex.a: Treat it as irregular and require stronger multi-factor authentication (e.g. OTP + biometrics) before allowing login, since the password may have been stolen.
ex.az: 属异常登入，要求更强的多重认证，因密码可能被盗。

cards.en:
Virtual currencies such as Bitcoin use a decentralised peer-to-peer payment network to operate without any banks or central authorities. Each user keeps a distributed ledger recording every transaction processed in the network. Parties called miners verify the validity of each transaction and gain bitcoins as a reward — this is Bitcoin mining.

Process: (1) Peter wants to give Daisy 1 bitcoin; (2) Peter signs the transaction with his own private key; (3) miners collect and validate transactions into a block; (4) the block is published and every distributed ledger is updated; (5) Daisy receives the bitcoin. Records are visible to everyone and cannot be tampered with or deleted.

NFT (Non-fungible Token) is an emerging virtual asset (digital artwork, in-game items). Each NFT contains unique information (creator, creation date) like an ID card, and ownership and transactions are verified through blockchain.
cards.zh:
比特币等虚拟货币用去中心化 P2P 网络运作，没有银行或中央机构。每个用户有 distributed ledger（分散式帐本）记录所有交易；miners 验证交易并获比特币奖励（mining）。
流程：Peter 用自己私钥签署交易 → miners 验证并组成 block → 发布并更新所有帐本 → Daisy 收到。纪录公开、不可篡改或删除。
NFT：新兴虚拟资产（数码艺术、游戏道具），含独特资讯如身份证，经区块链证明拥有权及交易。

ex.q: Why is it hard for one person to fake a Bitcoin transaction record?
ex.a: The ledger is distributed: every participant holds a copy and miners validate each block. Changing one copy would not match everyone else's ledger, so the fake record would be rejected.
ex.az: 帐本分散在所有参与者，miners 验证；改动一份与其他人不符会被拒绝。

mc.q: What is the main purpose of encryption?
o: Ensure data privacy if data is accessed illegally
mc.e: Encryption keeps content private; it does not stop interception.
mc.ez: 加密保障私隐，不阻止截取。

mc.q: Which is TRUE after a message is encrypted?
The original readable message is called
Decryption converts
Caesar cipher shift 3: encrypt 'CAT'.
Caesar cipher shift 3: decrypt 'LFW'.
How many combinations does a 24-bit key have?
A computer tries 1024 keys per second. Maximum time to crack a 20-bit key?
Why is a longer key more secure?
o: Data takes more time to transmit
Hackers need more time to try all keys
